Abraham is one of the [[three ancestors]] and the ancestor of Alpha

== Biblical narrative -> Gaiad narrative ==

=== Chapter 11 ===
When Terah's years reached seventy score,

He fathered Abram, Nahor, Haran, and more.

The line of Terah thus unfolds,

Of Abram, Nahor, Haran it holds.


Haran bore Lot, but life was brief,

In Ur of Chaldeans, he met with grief.

Abram wed Sarai, Nahor chose Milcah,

The daughters of Haran, both fair and tender.


Alas, poor Sarai, she bore no child,

Her womb was barren, fate unkind.

Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai dear,

To journey from Ur, a future unclear.


To Canaan's land, they sought to roam,

But Haran they found, and made it home.

Two hundred five years, Terah's days,

In Haran he passed, his final gaze.

=== Chapter 12 ===
The LORD to Abram spoke one day,

"Leave home and kin, I'll guide your way.

To lands unknown, I'll show the place,

A mighty nation shall embrace.

I'll bless you, Abram, make you great,

Your name revered, a blessed fate.

Those who bless you shall be blessed,

The ones who curse, shall face my test.

In you shall earth's great families see,

A blessing vast, for all to be."

So Abram went, as God decreed,

With Lot in tow, he paid due heed.

At seventy-five, from Haran's hold,

He took Sarai, possessions, bold.

To Canaan's land, they journeyed far,

Beneath the heavens, a guiding star.

In Canaan, Shechem's land they found,

Where Canaanites did then abound.

The LORD to Abram did appear,

"To your offspring, I'll give land near."

An altar there, to God he raised,

To mark the place, his voice he praised.

To Bethel's east, his tent he placed,

An altar built, God's name embraced.

Toward Negeb, Abram journeyed long,

His faith was steady, spirit strong.

A famine struck, the land did ail,

To Egypt's realm, they'd set their sail.

As Egypt's border Abram neared,

He spoke to Sarai, beauty revered.

"I know you're fair, a sight to see,

They'll want you, love, and murder me.

So say you are my sister, dear,

That I may live and have no fear."

In Egypt, all her beauty praised,

And to Pharaoh's house she was raised.

For her, they treated Abram well,

With livestock, slaves, his wealth did swell.

But God struck down with plagues severe,

On Pharaoh's house, for Sarai dear.

Then Pharaoh called to Abram near,

"Why have you done this? Made me fear?

Why claim her sister, not your bride?

I took her as my wife, you lied.

Now take your wife and go your way,

No longer here, you're free today."

Pharaoh's men sent him on his path,

With wife and wealth, he faced no wrath.

=== Chapter 13 ===
From Egypt, Abram journeyed on,

With wife and wealth, and Lot, his pawn.

To Negeb, he, his riches vast,

In livestock, silver, gold amassed.

From Negeb then, he traveled far,

To Bethel, where his roots once were.

Between Bethel and Ai he stood,

And called upon the Lord, the good.

With Abram, Lot did journey too,

His flocks and herds and tents he grew.

The land could not sustain them both,

Their wealth and strife, it seemed, did loathe.

The herders fought, Abram and Lot,

While Canaanites and Perizzites sought.

"Let there be peace," said Abram wise,

"For we are kin, let's not despise.

The land is vast, please choose your way,

I'll take what's left, and there we'll stay."

If Lot chose left, then right he'd fare,

If right, then left, in God's great care.

Lot gazed upon the Jordan's plain,

With waters lush, like Eden's reign,

Like Egypt's land, Zoar's domain,

Ere Sodom, Gomorrah met their bane.

He chose the Jordan, journeyed east,

From Abram's side, their bond released.

In Canaan, Abram found his stay,

While Lot in cities made his way.

In Sodom's midst, Lot pitched his tent,

Where wickedness and sin were spent.

The Lord then spoke to Abram dear,

"Now Lot is gone, your path is clear.

Look north and south, east and west,

All land you see shall be possessed.

Your offspring, like the dust, shall spread,

In numbers vast, as I have said.

Rise up and walk through breadth and length,

For in this land, I give you strength."

Abram moved to Mamre's oaks,

In Hebron's land, the altar stokes.

=== Chapter 14 ===
In days of old, four kings did reign,

Amraphel, Arioch, Chedorlaomer, Tidal's gain.

They waged a war, a fearsome fight,

'Gainst five kings, in their united might.

In Siddim's valley, by Dead Sea's shore,

Twelve years they served, but would no more.

In year thirteen, they dared rebel,

And fourteen saw retribution swell.

Chedorlaomer, kings in tow,

Subdued the lands where giants grow.

From Ashteroth to El-paran,

Their conquests spread, a vast expanse.

Then Sodom's king and Gomorrah's too,

Admah, Zeboiim, and Zoar's crew,

In Siddim's valley, waged their war,

Four kings 'gainst five, a fearsome score.

With bitumen pits, the valley lined,

The fleeing kings, some pits did find.

To hills they fled, their lands laid waste,

As enemies claimed their goods in haste.

They seized the wealth of Sodom's land,

And Gomorrah's spoils, they too, did brand.

They took Lot too, Abram's kin,

And all his goods, and vanished then.

A man escaped the fray and found

Abram the Hebrew, Mamre-bound.

He told of Lot, in captive state,

And of the kings who met their fate.

When Abram heard his nephew's plight,

He gathered men to join the fight.

Three hundred eighteen, strong and bold,

In hot pursuit, to Dan they rolled.

By night, they struck with stealth and speed,

Abram and servants, strong indeed.

They chased their foes to Hobah's land,

North of Damascus, victory at hand.

He rescued Lot, his nephew dear,

And all the goods, the spoils brought near.

The women, people, they set free,

A triumphant march, a jubilee.

The king of Sodom, grateful, came

To meet with Abram, praise his name.

In Shaveh's Valley, there they stood,

Where kings once gathered, now for good.

Melchizedek, of Salem's throne,

Brought bread and wine, to bless his own.

A priest of God Most High, he blessed

Abram, in victory's sweet success.

"By God Most High, let blessings flow,

To Abram, conqueror of his foe."

A tenth of all, to him was given,

As Abram honored God of heaven.

The king of Sodom made his plea,

"Give me the people, goods take thee."

But Abram swore by God Most High,

No thread or thong of his would lie.

"No wealth from you will I accept,

Lest you should claim, by you I'm kept."

Only the food his men consumed,

And shares for Aner, Eshcol, Mamre, resumed.

=== Chapter 15 ===
In vision, God to Abram spoke,

"Fear not, my shield protects thee, folk.

A great reward awaits for thee,

Trust in my word, and you shall see."

Yet Abram asked, "O Lord divine,

What gift is mine, when none's my line?

Eliezer, though he serves me well,

Inheritance in him won't dwell."

"You've granted me no child," he cried,

"And so, a slave must fill the tide."

But God replied, "This won't be so,

From your own blood, your heir shall grow."

God led him out, and bade him see

The stars above, in vast decree.

"Count them, if you can," said He,

"So shall your progeny soon be."

Abram believed, and in his heart,

He knew God's promise from the start.

For faith, as righteousness, was deemed,

And Abram's trust in God redeemed.

"I brought you forth from Ur," God said,

"To grant this land, where you shall tread."

But Abram asked, "How will I know

This land is mine, as you bestow?"

"Bring creatures young, of three years' time,

A heifer, goat, and ram to climb.

A turtledove and pigeon, too,

And I will show my word is true."

He brought them all, and split them down,

But left the birds uncut, uncrowned.

When prey descended from the skies,

Abram, with strength, drove them to flight.

As sun retired, and twilight reigned,

Deep sleep on Abram fell, constrained.

A darkness, vast and fearsome, crept,

And filled his heart with dread, inept.

The Lord declared, "Your offspring know,

In foreign land, as strangers grow.

Four centuries enslaved, confined,

Oppressed, but judgment waits behind.

The nation, cruel, shall feel my hand,

Your kin will leave with wealth so grand.

In peace, you'll join your kin, the past,

In ripe old age, your rest amassed.

The fourth generation shall return,

For Amorites' iniquity must burn."

The sun had set, the darkness hung,

A smoking pot and torch among

The severed parts, a sign divine,

God's covenant with Abram's line.

"To your descendants, I bequeath,

From Egypt's river, 'neath the wreath,

To Euphrates, vast and great,

These lands of tribes, I now relate:

Kenites, Kenizzites, the first,

Kadmonites too, shall quench their thirst.

The Hittites, Perizzites, as well,

Rephaim, their numbers shall swell.

Amorites, Canaanites, in part,

Girgashites, Jebusites, take heart.

Their lands I grant, a promise made,

My covenant with you displayed."

=== Chapter 16 ===
Sarai, Abram's wife, bore him no heir,

An Egyptian slave, Hagar, in their care.

Sarai spoke to Abram, filled with strife,

"The Lord withholds from me a fruitful life.

My slave, Hagar, may bear what I cannot,"

Abram heeded, as Sarai had thought.

Ten years in Canaan passed like a dream,

Sarai gave Hagar as wife, it would seem.

Abram with Hagar joined, she conceived,

Her mistress, Sarai, she now perceived.

Contempt she held, her bearing esteemed,

Sarai to Abram, her anger, it teemed.

"The wrong done to me falls on your head!

My slave in your arms, contempt she's bred.

Let God judge between us, my husband dear."

Abram replied, "She's yours, act without fear."

Sarai, relentless, drove Hagar away,

Into the wild, Hagar's path did sway.

An angel found her near a spring, so pure,

On the way to Shur, her fate unsure.

"Hagar, Sarai's slave, whence have you roamed?

From whence you came, and where is your home?"

"I flee from Sarai, my mistress unkind,"

Hagar replied, her destiny to find.

The angel spoke, "Return and to her yield,

Submit to her, your mistress, in the field.

Your offspring I will multiply, so vast,

In number, they'll be boundless, unsurpassed.

You shall bear a son, and Ishmael his name,

For God has seen your strife and heard your claim.

A wild ass of a man, he'll be at odds,

His hand 'gainst all, and all 'gainst him, the gods.

El-roi, she named the Lord, her vision clear,

"Have I seen God and yet I still am here?"

A well called Beer-lahai-roi was found,

'Twixt Kadesh and Bered, its fame renowned.

To Abram, Hagar bore a son, so blessed,

Ishmael, the child of promise, now confessed.

Eighty-six years of age, as time unfurled,

When Hagar bore to Abram his new world.

=== Chapter 17 ===
At ninety-nine, to Abram God appeared,

"I am the Lord Almighty," He declared,

"Walk 'fore me, blameless, in my sight abide,

And I'll make my covenant with you, my guide.

Exceeding numerous, you'll be renowned,

Then Abram fell upon his face, face-down.

God spoke, "This covenant I make with thee,

Ancestor to a multitude, you'll be.

No more shall Abram be the name you bear,

But Abraham, as nations rise from there,

For I have made you father to them all,

A multitude of nations shall you call."[[Category:Oldest pages before the refresh]]
